authorization.scope: P01 isolated Wayland menu input investigation

observations.advertised_input_protocols_scope: Filtered for the wayland-info client, whose desktop metadata does not request org_kde_kwin_fake_input; this was not an exhaustive compositor-global inventory.

interpretation.conclusion: The private --virtual session initially exposed a keyboard-only wl_seat to wayland-info. The absence of org_kde_kwin_fake_input in that client registry did not prove the compositor lacked the protocol: KWin filters this privileged interface per client desktop metadata. R627 registered an isolated probe with X-KDE-Wayland-Interfaces=org_kde_kwin_fake_input; KWin authorized it and exposed fake-input v5. Binding it added pointer capability to wl_seat (observed 2→3→7), removed again when destroyed (6→2).

next: Trace why authorized synthetic key/pointer events do not change the private Kicker QML state; do not infer hover or focus behavior from protocol advertisement alone.
Keep the R619 ordering hypothesis open until a native UI event trace or user-confirmed live observation correlates hover, focus, deactivation, and popup closure.
